oneLiner: A post-scandal AI-server pure play that just doubled its gross margin and guided FY2027 revenue roughly 26% above Street, yet trades near 11x forward earnings because the market does not fully trust the margins, the customers, or the controls.
thesis: The margin inflection finally showed up. Q4 FY2026 GAAP gross margin hit 17.5% versus 9.9% in Q3 FY26 and guidance of 8.2-8.4%, on favorable customer and product mix; non-GAAP EPS of $1.70 beat consensus $0.71 by 139%.
FY2027 guidance towers over consensus. Management guided $65-72B revenue versus Street ~$54.4B, backed by more than $60B of new orders received in Q4 alone and a record backlog.

Rack-scale liquid-cooling leadership into the Rubin cycle. DCBBS blueprints for NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72/NVL144 and DLC-2 direct liquid cooling (up to 362kW per rack) keep Supermicro first-to-market as DLC becomes mandatory at Rubin power densities.
The customer base is broadening. Nine customers each generated over $1B of revenue in FY2026, up from four in FY2025.
US-based manufacturing is a strategic asset. San Jose HQ, R&D and expanded domestic rack-scale capacity fit the onshoring policy environment and hyperscaler speed requirements.

latestProse: Q4 FY2026 (ended June 30, 2026, reported August 11) delivered revenue of $11.12B, up ~92% YoY, a slight miss versus the $11.73B consensus - but the story was margin: GAAP gross margin of 17.5% versus 9.9% in Q3 and its own 8.2-8.4% guide, driving GAAP EPS of $1.62 and non-GAAP EPS of $1.70 against a $0.71 estimate. Full-year FY2026 revenue was $39.1B (+78%) with non-GAAP EPS of $3.63. The disclosure that matters most: over $60B of new orders in a single quarter and nine $1B-plus customers (vs four in FY25) - evidence the backlog, not the quarter, now defines the stock.
guidanceProse: Management guided Q1 FY2027 revenue to $14.5-15.5B and full-year FY2027 to $65-72B, nearly 30% above the ~$54.4B consensus, implying revenue roughly at Dell's ISG scale within a year. The debate is whether Q4's 17.5% gross margin was a mix-driven spike (a few rich rack-scale deals) or a durable step-change; BofA and Goldman stayed cautious on margin sustainability even while the Street raised targets. Explicit FY27 margin guidance: unverified.
segments: Server and storage systems are the overwhelming majority of revenue, subsystems/accessories the small remainder
AI/GPU rack-scale platforms are the growth engine; management has cited AI platforms as the large majority of revenue
Concentration: in Q3 FY26 one datacenter customer was 27% of revenue; nine customers each exceeded $1B for FY2026
competitive: Dell (ISG) and HPE bundle AI servers with services and financing and drove the price competition that held SMCI gross margin near 9-10% through FY25; Q4's 17.5% reflects mix, not a truce
ODMs (Quanta, Wiwynn, Foxconn) serve hyperscalers directly at thin margins and cap pricing on the biggest deals
NVIDIA allocation is the real gatekeeper: Supermicro ships GB300 at volume and has announced Vera Rubin NVL72/NVL144 support with DCBBS blueprints scaling 5MW to 1GW
Differentiators are time-to-market cadence, building-block architecture, DLC-2 cooling scale, and US manufacturing
moat: There is little structural moat in assembling x86/GPU servers; Dell, HPE and ODMs can replicate most of the portfolio, which is why gross margin historically sat near 10%. Supermicro's edge is speed - first-to-market on each NVIDIA generation - plus rack-scale DLC integration at volume. That is a lead measured in quarters, not years.
risks: Margin mean reversion. A gross margin that doubled in one quarter on customer mix can halve the same way; guidance credibility rests on repeating it, and top analysts openly doubt it.

The governance overhang is not resolved. Material weaknesses in internal controls remained unremediated as of March 31, 2026, BDO issued an adverse ICFR opinion on FY2024, DOJ/SEC document subpoenas remain outstanding, and a March 19, 2026 DOJ indictment charged two employees and a contractor over alleged export-control violations (company not charged).
Customer concentration and order quality. One customer was 27% of Q3 FY26 revenue; the $60B order book is only as good as hyperscaler follow-through.
Competition and allocation. Any shift in NVIDIA allocation toward Dell, HPE or ODMs on the Rubin ramp directly hits the FY27 guide.
Working capital strain. Funding $65-72B of revenue requires massive inventory and receivables build, with dilution or debt risk if cash conversion lags.
Blackwell-to-Rubin transition air pocket. Customers pausing GB300 purchases ahead of Vera Rubin could create an inventory-heavy dead quarter.
catalysts: Late Aug 2026: FY2026 10-K filing - ICFR opinion, remediation progress, concentration disclosure
2H CY2026 into CY2027: Vera Rubin NVL72/NVL144 volume shipments
No set timetable: conclusion of the independent board investigation
pricedIn: The stock jumped 17.6% to $37.15 on Aug 12, 2026 after the print, and the forward P/E sits near 11x - far below AI-hardware peers. The price implies the market discounts both the $65-72B guide and the 17.5% margin: taking guidance at face value with even 14-15% gross margins would make the stock cheap outright. The debate is binary - durable margin regime plus real backlog versus a mix-driven one-off from a company with unremediated material weaknesses.

scenarios.bear: Gross margin reverts toward 10-12% as the mix normalizes and Dell/HPE/ODM price pressure returns, FY27 revenue lands nearer $55B, and the investigation or a delayed 10-K reignites the accounting discount; EPS stalls near $4 and the multiple compresses toward 8x - low $30s or below.
scenarios.base: Revenue lands in the lower half of the $65-72B guide with gross margins settling in the 12-14% range, non-GAAP EPS in the $5-6 area for FY27, filings stay current and the investigation closes without company charges; at 10-12x the stock grinds toward the $55-70 range.
scenarios.bull: Rubin-cycle DLC leadership and enterprise mix keep gross margins at 15%+, revenue reaches the $70B+ end, EPS approaches $7-8, and governance normalization re-rates the multiple toward 14-16x - a roughly $100+ stock.

valPresets.note: Basis is forward earnings: FCF whipsaws with working-capital swings in a pass-through hardware model. The 12% discount rate carries the governance overhang; at ~11x forward, the reverse DCF shows how little growth is priced.
